objects.title: Temple of Portunus
objects.note: The standing temple, modelled in the catalogue. Footprint is the present-day OpenStreetMap outline; the model itself is drawn from a historic plan (see its own evidence card).

objects.title: Temple of Hercules Victor
objects.note: The standing round temple, modelled in the catalogue. Footprint is the present-day OpenStreetMap outline; its original roof is lost.

objects.title: Pons Aemilius
objects.note: Position from the surviving Ponte Rotto arch (two piers fixed at E -134.5 and -105.6 m); stone, seven spans (Wikipedia). The other pier positions, the deck width and the arch profile are guessed so the bridge meets today's banks.

objects.title: River quay · Portus Tiberinus frontage
objects.note: A stone-faced river wall with steps, set along today's east bank of the Tiber (an approximation of the ancient bank, not its course). That Rome's river harbour had built quays is likely, but no source here records this stretch.

objects.title: River quay · south of the bridge
objects.note: A stone-faced river wall with steps, set along today's east bank of the Tiber (an approximation of the ancient bank, not its course). That Rome's river harbour had built quays is likely, but no source here records this stretch.

objects.title: Riverside road
objects.note: A road running along the quay behind the river wall. Its line is today's east bank offset inland; nothing records it, so it is a guess.

objects.title: Road from the bridge to the Velabrum
objects.note: Platner records a road leading from the bridge across the Forum Boarium towards the Velabrum. The route is bent here to pass north of the Temple of Portunus; its exact line is a guess.

objects.title: Vicus Tuscus · Forum end
objects.note: The line OpenStreetMap maps for the Vicus Tuscus at its Forum end (Pleiades locates it to about 20 m). Width and paving are guessed.

objects.title: Vicus Tuscus · through the Velabrum to the market
objects.note: Pleiades and Wikipedia say the street ran from the Forum along the western flank of the Palatine, through the Velabrum, to the Forum Boarium (processions went this way to the Circus). Its exact line is guessed along today's Via di San Teodoro and Via del Velabro, which lie in the same valley.

objects.title: Vicus Iugarius · Forum end
objects.note: The line OpenStreetMap maps for the Vicus Iugarius near the Forum. Pleiades says it led from the Forum to the Porta Carmentalis. Width and paving are guessed.

objects.title: Vicus Iugarius · foot of the Capitoline to the market
objects.note: Platner names the Vicus Iugarius as a route into the Forum Boarium and Pleiades has it leaving by the Porta Carmentalis. Its line along the foot of the Capitoline is guessed from today's Via della Consolazione and Via del Velabro.

objects.title: Clivus Victoriae
objects.note: The steep street up the Palatine, on the line OpenStreetMap maps for it (Pleiades locates it to about 20 m). Width and paving are guessed.

objects.title: Road from the market to the Circus Maximus
objects.note: The Forum Boarium opened towards the starting gates of the Circus Maximus (Platner, Wikipedia). The road is likely; its line is guessed along today's Via dei Cerchi.

objects.title: Road west of the bridge into Trastevere
objects.note: The Pons Aemilius led over the river to the west bank. A road continuing from the bridge is likely; its line and width are guessed.

objects.title: Circus Maximus
objects.note: The long axis and extent are fitted to the OpenStreetMap outline of the excavated site (596 m long); the track is 118 m wide and the whole circus about 621 m long (Wikipedia). Seating, the central barrier with Augustus's obelisk, the starting gates and the outer arcade are massing only: the depth of the stands, tier heights and the 24 m outer wall are guessed. Trajan's stone rebuilding began just after AD 100.

objects.title: Domus Flavia · imperial palace (public wing)
objects.note: Position and size fitted to the surviving walls OpenStreetMap maps (152 by 100 m); completed about AD 92 by Domitian (Pleiades, Wikipedia). Wall height (the rooms about 18 m; the great hall over 30 m, with a 30.6 m span) follows Wikipedia. The courtyard, the hall's place and every roof and facade are massing, not a reconstruction.

objects.title: Domus Augustana · imperial palace (residential wing)
objects.note: Position and size fitted to the surviving walls OpenStreetMap maps (225 by 86 m); the central block of Domitian's palace, finished about AD 92, with two peristyles and a great curved exedra facing the Circus Maximus (Wikipedia). Heights, the courts and the exedra's size are massing, guessed.

objects.title: Domus Tiberiana · imperial palace (north-west corner of the Palatine)
objects.note: The platform at the north-west corner of the hill, fitted to the walls OpenStreetMap maps (220 by 120 m); Wikipedia gives about 150 by 120 m and arcaded supports on the north slope, rebuilt under Domitian. Its height and courtyard are massing, guessed.

objects.title: Forum Boarium · open paved square
objects.note: The cattle market was an open public space (Platner, Wikipedia). The present-day site outline is widened slightly here to give an open square; the true ancient extent is not recorded, and its surface (paving) is a guess.

objects.title: Ara Maxima of Hercules
objects.note: Placed at Pleiades' derived point for the altar; its foundations are tentatively a tuff platform in the crypt of Santa Maria in Cosmedin. Size, steps and the altar block are guessed.

insula.title: Insula · shops below, flats above
insula.note: A multi-storey block of flats with shops (tabernae) along the ground floor, the usual form in Roman streets (Wikipedia, Insula). Heights stay under the Roman limit of about 17.75 m. That a block stood here, and its size and height, are guesses.

flats.title: Block of flats (insula)
flats.note: A multi-storey block of flats, typical of the dense streets and courtyards of Roman districts (Wikipedia, Insula). Heights stay under the Roman limit of about 17.75 m. That a block stood here, and its size, are guesses.

shop.title: Shop-house (taberna) with rooms above
shop.note: A shop with a wide opening at street level and rooms above, the usual form in Roman streets (Wikipedia, Insula). That a shop stood here is a guess; so are its size and height.

warehouse.title: Riverside warehouse (horreum)
warehouse.note: A two-storey warehouse with thick walls and few, high windows (Wikipedia, Horrea). Riverside storage near the harbour is likely; this building's place and size are guessed.

lane.title: Back lane
lane.note: A narrow lane between blocks, the usual fine grain of Roman districts (Wikipedia, Insula). That a lane ran here, and its width, are guesses; the lines are laid out by the generator, not recorded.
